_comment: Single source of truth for move-classification constants. Loaded by server/app/analysis.py and bundled into the client via client/src/lib/classification.ts — edit here, never in the consumers. A move is graded by how much it lowers the mover's winning chances: win% = 50 + 50 * (2 / (1 + exp(-winPercentK * cp)) - 1), the curve Lichess fits to its games, with cp clamped to evalClampCp. Threshold upper bounds are exclusive drops in win% points: a drop < 1 is best, 1-2.5 good, etc.; at or past the last bound is a blunder. They are set so a level position grades as the old centipawn bars did (10/25/50/100 cp come to 0.9/2.3/4.6/9.2 points at 0.00), while a pawn given away at +6 barely moves the needle. Forced mates are graded on their own terms (mateLost, mateCreated) and a book move is 'book' unless it is a blunder. The server's test_classification.py pins the canonical values; shared/classification-cases.json is the conformance table.
_mateComment: Lichess's mate rules, from the mover's side. mateLost: the mover had a forced mate and no longer does; graded by the eval left over (above inaccuracyAboveCp: inaccuracy, above mistakeAboveCp: mistake, else blunder). mateCreated: the opponent has a forced mate that they did not have before; graded by how lost the mover already was (below -inaccuracyAboveCp: inaccuracy, below -mistakeAboveCp: mistake, else blunder).
